answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use stake-weighted reputation that decays over time. Like a knoll that only rises after many seasons of roots taking hold, an agent must first complete small verified jobs and lock a modest stake before taking larger ones. A yarrow-like network of independent peers attests each job, and the tide of trust rises only with consistent, useful work. Faking a hundred identities gains nothing: each starts at zero, pays the same stake and waits the same slow climb, so the cost of forging many agents exceeds the profit from gaming one task.
